title: Poems at the bus stop
summary: Someone is leaving short poems at a bus stop every morning, and the passengers start to answer.
paragraphs: It started on a Tuesday in January. At the bus stop outside the hospital, someone had stuck a small card on the {{timetable}}. On it, in neat handwriting, were three lines: "The bus is late again. / The sky is the colour of milk. / I am not in a hurry." There was no name.

Most people didn't notice. But Rosa, a cleaner who caught the 6.40 bus every morning, read it twice and smiled. The next day there was another card: "A man runs for the bus. / His coffee runs faster. / We all wait for him." Rosa laughed out loud, and a man next to her asked what was so funny. She showed him. He laughed too.

Every morning there was a new poem. Some were funny, some were a little sad, and they were all about small things: the rain, a dog that waited with its owner, the smell of bread from the bakery across the road. People began arriving early to read them. They took photos and shared them. {{Strangers}} who had waited at the same stop for years started to talk to each other.

Then, one morning, somebody {{replied}}. Under the poem there was a second card in different handwriting: "Thank you. / My mother is in this hospital. / Your words help me wait." After that, more people wrote replies. Soon the timetable was covered in cards, and the bus company had to put up a special {{board}} next to the stop so that the timetable could still be read.

Nobody ever found out who wrote the first poems. Rosa has an idea: she once saw an elderly man with a pencil behind his ear getting off the night bus at five in the morning. But she has never asked him. "If I ask, it will stop being a {{mystery}}," she says. "And I like the mystery." Every Friday now, she leaves a poem of her own.

timetable.meaning: a list of the times when buses or trains arrive and leave

board.meaning: a flat piece of wood or plastic where you can put notices

mystery.meaning: something strange that nobody can explain

questions.question: Where were the poems?
options: On the timetable at a bus stop outside a hospital
On the door of the bakery
questions.explanation: Someone stuck a small card on the timetable at the bus stop outside the hospital.

questions.question: What were the poems about?
questions.explanation: They were all about small things: the rain, a dog, the smell of bread.

questions.question: Why did the bus company put up a board?
options: Because the cards were covering the timetable
Because the hospital asked them to
questions.explanation: The timetable was covered in cards, so they added a board so it could still be read.

questions.question: Why doesn't Rosa ask the man who she thinks wrote the poems?
options: She wants it to stay a mystery.
She thinks he would be angry.
questions.explanation: She says if she asks, it will stop being a mystery, and she likes the mystery.
